full_content:
Lovely Professional University (LPU) hosted 
"The Creator Economy: Behind the Screen -- From Content to Career,"
 an engaging event that explored the evolving landscape of content creation and the growing opportunities in the digital creator economy.

Featuring creators Jomedy, Mohit Puri, Ravleen Kaur, Riya Arora, Zeenat, Priyanshu Dogra, and Kartik Wadhwa, the event offered insights into how creativity, passion, and consistency can help individuals build careers in the digital space.

The discussions highlighted the changing dynamics of the creator economy, where content creation extends beyond entertainment to offer opportunities for personal branding, audience engagement, collaboration, and professional growth. The event provided a platform to explore the possibilities of transforming creative interests into sustainable career pathways.

Through such initiatives, LPU continues to provide students with opportunities to explore emerging industries, gain fresh perspectives, and understand the evolving career landscape.

The event celebrated the power of creativity and the potential of digital content to shape new professional opportunities.

title: LPU Hosts International Conference on Multi-Functional Advanced Materials (MAM-2026), Advancing Research and Innovation for a Sustainable Future
full_content:
Lovely Professional University (LPU) successfully organised the International Conference on Multi-Functional Advanced Materials (MAM-2026) on 16-17 October 2026. Organised by the Department of Research Impact and Outcome (DRIO), Research and Development Cell, LPU. The two-day international conference brought together eminent academicians, global researchers, industry experts, and distinguished keynote speakers to discuss emerging advancements in multifunctional materials and their applications.

The conference was graced by 
Dr. Col. Rashmi Mittal, Pro Chancellor, LPU
, whose visionary leadership and encouragement reinforced the university's commitment to research, innovation, and academic excellence. The event received further support from Prof. (Dr.) Lovi Raj Gupta, Pro Vice Chancellor; Dr. Aman Mittal, Vice President, LPU; Er. H. R. Singla, Director General, LPU; Prof. (Dr.) Atul Thakur, Dean, Research and Development Cell; and Prof. (Dr.) Hitesh Vasudev, Head, Department of Research Impact and Outcome.

The conference also welcomed distinguished guests, including Prof. Niraj Bala, Professor and Dean, NITTTR, Chandigarh; Dr. Satish Kumar, Professor and Dean, Research & Consultancy, NIT Jamshedpur; and Dr. Darren Player, Associate Professor, Division of Surgery and Interventional Science, University College London (UCL), United Kingdom. Their participation and expert perspectives contributed to meaningful academic discussions and strengthened international research engagement.

The keynote sessions featured prominent experts from leading national and international institutions. The speakers included Dr. Ganga Ram Chaudhary from Panjab University; Dr. Radha Raman Mishra from BITS Pilani; Dr. Tannishtha Devgun from the University of Padua, Italy; and Dr. Preeti Thakur from Amity University Haryana. The second day continued with insightful keynote addresses by Prof. Yassine Slimani from LAFBU, Saudi Arabia; Dr. Arijit Chowdhuri from the University of Delhi; and Dr. Lalit Thakur from NIT Kurukshetra.

Throughout the two-day event, participants explored emerging developments in advanced materials, their functional properties, and their potential industrial applications. The conference provided a dynamic platform for presenting innovative research, exchanging scientific knowledge, fostering interdisciplinary collaboration, and discussing technological solutions to contemporary challenges.

MAM-2026 highlighted the growing importance of multifunctional advanced materials in driving scientific progress and supporting sustainable technological development. By bringing together researchers, academic leaders, and industry experts, the conference encouraged knowledge sharing and collaboration across disciplines and institutions.

Through initiatives such as MAM-2026, Lovely Professional University continues to strengthen its research ecosystem, promote international academic partnerships, and advance impactful research and technological innovation aimed at building a sustainable future.

title: 56 LPU Faculty among the World's Top 2% Scientists in 2026, 23 Ranked in the Top 100 Research Subfields
full_content:
* 

9 faculty members rank among the top 50 in their respective subfields, while 12 earn recognition for their career

long research impact.

Lovely Professional University (LPU) has strengthened its position as a global centre of research, since 56 of its faculty are included in the world's top 2% of scientists according to the 2026 Stanford-Elsevier rankings. This acknowledgement shows that the university is making an increasing contribution to scientific progress in a variety of fields, as 23 faculty members appear in the top 100 and 9 in the top 50 of their individual research areas. Moreover, 12 of the university's faculty have been recognised in the career long impact rankings, indicating the long-term impact of their research.

The Stanford-Elsevier rankings evaluate researchers using standardised citation indicators, H-index, and other measures of research impact. LPU's latest achievement reflects both the breadth of its research ecosystem and the growing visibility of its faculty's scholarly contributions at the global level.

Congratulating the achievers, Dr. Ashok Kumar Mittal, Member of Parliament (Rajya Sabha) and Founder Chancellor of LPU, stated, "This achievement reflects the dedication of researchers of LPU who continue to expand the frontiers of knowledge through their work. Strong research institutions play a vital role in a nation's progress, and sustained investment in research is essential to building scientific capabilities, encouraging innovation and finding solutions to complex challenges. Such accomplishments strengthen India's research standing and open new possibilities for future generations of scholars."

The 56 recognised faculty members represent 22 research subfields, with the highest representation in Pharmacology & Pharmacy (9), Plant Biology & Botany (7), Artificial Intelligence & Image Processing (6), Food Science (5), and Optoelectronics & Photonics (5). Other represented fields include Biotechnology (3), Materials (2), Applied Physics (2), Legal & Forensic Medicine (2), Environmental Sciences, Neurology & Neurosurgery, Nuclear & Particle Physics, Polymers, Business & Management, Chemical Physics, Organic Chemistry, Chemical Engineering, Biochemistry & Molecular Biology, General Physics, Networking & Telecommunications, Medicinal & Biomolecular Chemistry, and Biophysics.

Further underscoring LPU's research depth, nine faculty members ranked among the top 50 in their respective subfields. These included three in Optoelectronics & Photonics, two in Legal & Forensic Medicine, and one each in Pharmacology & Pharmacy, Plant Biology & Botany, Chemical Engineering, and Biophysics. Meanwhile, 23 faculty members featured among the top 100, with strong representation from Pharmacology & Pharmacy, Plant Biology & Botany, Optoelectronics & Photonics, Biotechnology, and Legal & Forensic Medicine, alongside Business & Management, Chemical Engineering, Biochemistry & Molecular Biology, Medicinal & Biomolecular Chemistry, Food Science, and Artificial Intelligence & Image Processing.

The recognition extends to the career long impact rankings, where 12 LPU faculty members represent 10 research domains. Food Science and Materials account for two faculty members each, while Nuclear & Particle Physics, Polymers, Neurology & Neurosurgery, Environmental Sciences, Organic Chemistry, Pharmacology & Pharmacy, Plant Biology & Botany, and Optoelectronics & Photonics account for one each. Their inclusion highlights research contributions that have sustained influence over the course of their scientific careers.

Research has remained central to LPU's academic vision for more than 25 years, with the university continuing to strengthen its research infrastructure, scholarly output, intellectual property creation and global collaborations. This commitment is reflected in its recent performance in the Times Higher Education (THE) World University Rankings 2027, where LPU ranked first among private universities in India for Research Environment, fourth in India and 161st globally for Research Quality. The university has also earned international recognition at the THE Awards Asia 2026, winning in the Research Project of the Year: Arts, Humanities and Social Sciences category for its research on Kerala's tribal communities. Supported by more than 34,500+ publications, over 4,25,000+ Scopus citations, a Scopus H-index of 204, more than 3,200 granted intellectual property rights and over Rs. 98.35 crore in funded projects, LPU's research record reflects a sustained effort to generate knowledge, address real-world challenges and contribute to scientific and societal progress.

title: LPU's Ecological Restoration Efforts with 8,572 Seed Balls and 130 km of Green Corridors Earn Platinum Green Impact Award from National EduTrust of India
full_content:
* 

422 students, 11 tree species and five geo tagged sites across three Punjab districts turn a campus sustainability initiative into a documented ecological action

Lovely Professional University (LPU) has received the Platinum Green Impact Award 2026, the highest recognition under the Seed Balls for Sustainable Campuses Initiative 2026 organised by the National EduTrust of India (NEI). The nationwide campaign invited higher education institutions to prepare and responsibly disperse seed balls containing tree seeds as a practical exercise in biodiversity conservation, ecological restoration and environmental education. As part of the initiative, LPU prepared 8,572 seed balls using 11 tree species, involving 422 students, and dispersed them across five geo-tagged locations spanning Kapurthala, Amritsar and Shaheed Bhagat Singh Nagar districts of Punjab.

LPU's participation is particularly significant because of the ecological composition of the seed balls. Of the total 8,572 prepared, 7,643 seed balls, or 89.2 per cent, used native species, while 929, or 10.8 per cent, used naturalised species. Native species included Karanj, Shisham, Amaltas, Kachnar, Moringa, Kadam, Jamun, and Arjun, while naturalised species included Imli, Gulmohar, and Pink Shower.

The campaign was designed by NEI to take environmental learning beyond awareness and into direct participation. Students and faculty were encouraged to understand local tree species, prepare seed balls using natural materials, and disperse them at ecologically suitable locations. The initiative formed part of a larger nationwide effort involving around 350 institutions, which collectively prepared more than 10 lakh seed balls and dispersed approximately 8 lakh of them.

Dr. Ashok Kumar Mittal, Member of Parliament (Rajya Sabha) and Founder Chancellor of LPU, stated, "Sustainability cannot remain an idea discussed within classrooms or captured only in institutional reports, it must find its way into the soil, the communities and the choices we make every day. This prestigious award is encouraging because it recognises this spirit of participation, but more importantly, it reinforces a vision of education where knowledge is connected with responsibility towards nature and society".

At LPU, the activity extended beyond the university campus into different ecological settings. Of the 8,572 seed balls prepared, 6,072 were dispersed at field sites, while 2,500 were distributed through Green Gift packets. The documented dispersal sites included the LPU campus and adjoining areas in Phagwara, the AH1 Corridor in Kapurthala, Budha Theh near Beas, Lahorimal on the AH1 Corridor in Amritsar and the Chandigarh Jalandhar Expressway at Balachaur. Together, these sites covered approximately 130 kilometres of green corridors, including campus green belts, highway green belts, riverine embankments, roadside verges and expressway green belts.

The initiative engaged students from across 27 academic schools, with 422 students participating in the seed activity. Alongside the dispersal exercise, five awareness activities were conducted to connect the practical work with wider conversations around environmental responsibility, biodiversity and climate action.

The Platinum Green Impact Award 2026 adds a ground-level dimension to this 25-year journey, translating LPU's broader sustainability vision into direct student participation and ecological action. Earlier in 2026, LPU was also recognised in the Times Higher Education Sustainability Impact Rankings 2026, where it was placed 23rd globally and emerged as the highest ranked institution in India for its contribution towards the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals. Together, these recognitions reflect an approach to sustainability that spans institutional infrastructure, education, biodiversity, and measurable action on the ground.

title: Celebrating 25 Years of LPU Excellence and 5 Years of AICGS! Embracing Cultures, Inspiring Global Togetherness

title: Dr. Ashok Kumar Mittal Brings Together Leaders, Faith Traditions, Country Ambassadors and Sporting Champions at 'Seva Sankalp - Rashtranirman Ke 25 Saal'
full_content:
*
 A national gathering in New Delhi marks 25 years of governance under the leadership of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi; Asian Games champions felicitated for bringing glory to India

A powerful confluence of faith, public service, national responsibility and sporting excellence marked 'Seva Sankalp- Rashtranirman Ke 25 Saal', a national celebration marking 25 years of Prime Minister Narendra Modi's public life and journey of governance.

Convened by Dr. Ashok Kumar Mittal, Member of Parliament, Rajya Sabha, the event brought together distinguished public representatives, faith leaders, youth, cultural voices and sporting champions to reflect on the larger themes of seva, harmony, good governance and nation building.

The gathering witnessed the presence of elite political guests, Shri Sandeep Pathak, Member of Parliament, Rajya Sabha, Shri Jagdambika Pal, Member of Parliament, Lok Sabha, Shri Sanjay Goyal, Member of the Delhi Legislative Assembly (MLA), Shahdara, Shri Deepak Mhaskey, National Social Media Convenor, BJP, and Dr. Ashwin Fernandes, Chair, QS India and Vice President, Strategic and International Engagement, QS, along with several other distinguished guests.

The evening brought together representatives of different faith traditions on a common platform, reinforcing the message of India's pluralism and shared national purpose. The programme featured multifaith prayers, reflections on service and public responsibility, a documentary presentation and cultural performances.

The gathering brought together prominent spiritual and faith leaders representing diverse traditions, including Shri Marazban Nariman Zaiwalla, Trustee, Delhi Parsi Anjuman, Yog Manishi Acharya Shri Vivek Muni Ji Maharaj, Founder, Acharya Sushil Muni Mission, Giani Dilbagh Singh Ji, Head Granthi, Gurdwara Rakab Ganj Sahib, Swami Rajeshwara Nand Ji, Chairman, Sant Samaj Dal, Goswami Sushil Ji Maharaj, National Convenor, Bhartiya Sarva Dharma Sansad, Sahibzada Jia Nizami, Sahibzada Hazrat Nizamuddin Dargah, Bhante Dipankara Sumedho, Chairman, Buddhist Cultural Foundation India, and Mrs Carmel Tripathi, Director, Baha'i Office of Public Affairs.

Their participation underscored the central message of Seva Sankalp, that India's diversity of faiths can come together in a shared spirit of seva, harmony, compassion and national responsibility, values that have been central to Prime Minister Narendra Modi ji's vision of a united, inclusive and progressive Bharat.

Representatives of various diplomatic missions were also present, with delegations from countries including Nicaragua, Chad, Burundi, Liberia, Madagascar, Jordan, Russia, Cameroon, Botswana, Lesotho, Venezuela, Angola, Burkina Faso, Niger and Israel.

A major highlight of the evening was the felicitation of Indian athletes who brought laurels to the country at the 2026 Asian Games. The athletes were felicitated by Dr. Ashok Kumar Mittal along with senior dignitaries. The ceremony celebrated their dedication, discipline and contribution to India's sporting achievements.

Among the athletes honoured were Neeru Dhanda, Aman Sehrawat, Antim Panghal, Sujeet Kalkal, Kamaljeet, Nitesh Siwach, Pooja Singh, Kiran Pahal, Satnam Singh, Manisha Keer, Himanshu Dhillon, Sakshi Rana and Salman Khan. The athletes represented achievements across shooting, wrestling, athletics, rowing and hockey, among other sporting disciplines.

Speaking at the gathering, Dr Ashok Kumar Mittal, Member of Parliament, Rajya Sabha, said, "For me, this is not merely a celebration; it is a yagna to remember the 25-year journey of a man who has devoted a very large part of his life to public service. From Gujarat to Delhi, the journey of Narendra Modi ji has been one of public responsibility, trust and service.

The last 25 years give us much to remember and celebrate, but our eyes must also be on the next 25. Today, from India Gate, we salute the journey so far and make a collective resolve for a developed, stronger and globally leading India. For the next 25 years, we will do it."

The event also featured the launch of a song commemorating 25 years of governance, followed by a youth led Seva Sankalp pledge. Seven selected young participants led the pledge, underscoring the responsibility of the next generation in carrying forward the values of service and nation-building.

The evening concluded with 'Sounds of Seva', a live musical presentation celebrating India's diverse cultural and spiritual traditions. The programme brought the formal ceremony to a close on a note of unity and collective celebration.

The gathering sought to underline a simple but powerful message: India's strength lies in its diversity, but its future is shaped by the willingness of its people to come together in service of the nation.

title: LPU Athletes Contributed 62% of India's Gold Medal Haul at Asian Games 2026 in AichiNagoya, Japan
full_content:
* 

LPU's Neeru Dhanda scripted history with two golds and a silver in shooting, became India's first woman to win an individual Asian Games Gold in Trap Shooting, and was named flag

bearer for the Closing Ceremony

* 

32 LPU Students Won 28 Medals, including 13 Gold, 11 Silver, and 4 Bronze, as LPU Makes a Defining Contribution to India's Asian Games 2026 Campaign

The Indian sporting campaign at the 20th Asian Games in Aichi Nagoya concluded with a significant contribution from Lovely Professional University (LPU), as 32 LPU students collectively secured 28 medals, comprising 13 gold, 11 silver, and 4 bronze medals across nine sporting disciplines. The LPU contingent accounted for 62% of India's gold medals, 41% of its silver medals, and 11% of its bronze medals, contributing nearly one third of India's overall medal tally.

Representing India across 15 disciplines, 58 LPU students formed part of the country's Asian Games contingent. Their medal winning performances came in shooting, archery, hockey, wrestling, athletics, rowing, boxing, cricket, and weightlifting, reflecting a wide sporting footprint extending from precision sports and combat disciplines to team events and athletics.

The campaign was further elevated by an exceptional performance from LPU student and Indian trap shooter Neeru Dhanda, who secured two gold medals and a silver medal in shooting. She created history by becoming the first Indian woman to win an individual Asian Games gold medal in trap shooting, adding a significant chapter to India's shooting campaign in Aichi Nagoya. Her achievement was followed by another national honour, as Dhanda was named India's flag bearer for the closing ceremony of the Asian Games 2026, placing an LPU student at the forefront of India's representation at the conclusion of the continental sporting event.

The gold medal campaign was led by outstanding performances across multiple sporting arenas. Taniparthi Chikitha and Sahil Rajesh Jadhav won two gold medals each in compound archery. Aman Sehrawat won gold in men's freestyle 57 kg wrestling, Sujeet Kalkal secured gold in men's freestyle 65 kg wrestling, Lovlina Borgohain won gold in the women's 75 kg boxing event, and Kiran Pahal was part of India's gold medal winning women's 4×400 m relay team.

Team events added some of the most significant moments to the campaign. Seven LPU students were part of India's gold medal winning men's hockey team, while Sakshi Rana was part of the women's hockey team that secured gold. Ishan Kishan was also part of India's gold medal winning cricket team. The three gold medal victories involving LPU students also secured India's qualification for the LA 2028 Olympic Games, with the compound mixed team archery gold earning two quota places and the men's and women's hockey victories securing direct qualification for India.

The medal haul extended well beyond the gold medals. Bommadevara Dhiraj, Elavenil Valarivan and Himanshu Dhillon won two silver medals each, while Vidarsa K Vinod and Neeraj Chauhan also secured multiple medals. Saikhom Mirabai Chanu won silver in women's 49 kg weightlifting, while Antim Panghal and Nitesh Siwach added silver medals in wrestling. Bronze medals came through Neeraj Chauhan, Pooja Singh, Dharmveer Choudhary, Salman Khan and Satnam Singh.

Dr Ashok Kumar Mittal, Member of Parliament (Rajya Sabha) and Founder Chancellor of LPU, stated, "This achievement reflects the larger purpose of education, which is to nurture individuals who can create pride for the nation through their talent, discipline and determination. At LPU, we envision an ecosystem where young people are encouraged not only to pursue their own aspirations but also to contribute meaningfully to the nation's progress and standing on the world stage. Seeing our students carry the Indian flag with distinction is a matter of immense pride and a powerful reflection of that vision. Their journey inspires us to continue building opportunities where excellence, ambition, and national contribution go hand in hand."

LPU's medal winning performances spanned nine disciplines, with shooting leading the tally with 9 medals, followed by archery with 6, wrestling with 4, athletics with 3, hockey with 2, and boxing, cricket, rowing, and weightlifting contributing 1 medal each.

With 13 gold, 11 silver, and 4 bronze medals, the 2026 Asian Games marked one of the most significant international sporting performances by LPU students.  LPU's education and elite sport have increasingly converged to create pathways for young Indian athletes to compete at the highest level. From Olympic representation to Asian Games podium finishes, LPU athletes have continued to carry the Indian flag into major international arenas.

title: Record Participation of 6,000+ Innovators and 900+ Teams Marked LPU's Gear UP Season 5 Ahead of Smart India Hackathon

title: Engineers' Day Celebrated at LPU with a Focus on Innovation and Excellence
full_content:
On Engineers' Day, LPU focus is increasingly on how university can equip students to solve real world problems, gain industry exposure and build careers that contribute to India's technological and industrial growth.

title: LPU's GyanDeep Takes Education Beyond Classrooms on International Literacy Day
full_content:
* 

On International Literacy Day, LPU highlights its sustained education outreach, from teaching underprivileged children and promoting computer literacy to career guidance for over 80,000 school students

For some children, a classroom is a daily reality. For others, simply having access to books, a teacher, or a computer can be a life changing opportunity. This gap is where Lovely Professional University (LPU) is trying to make a difference through GyanDeep, a student led initiative that takes education from the university campus into nearby villages and underserved communities.

On International Literacy Day, the initiative offers a reminder that literacy is not only about being able to read and write. It is also about having the confidence to learn, access information, use technology, make informed choices, and imagine possibilities beyond one's immediate circumstances.

Under GyanDeep, LPU NSS volunteers regularly engage with children from low income communities, including those living in nearby slum areas and villages, providing supplementary education through interactive and activity based sessions. More than 250 children have been educated through the initiative, with 75 currently enrolled. What makes the programme distinctive is that LPU students themselves become teachers and mentors, taking lessons in subjects and skills while encouraging children to participate through storytelling, poetry, art, dance, and other creative activities.

The effort also extends to digital literacy. For children and villagers who may have little or no exposure to computers, LPU NSS volunteers conduct free basic computer training both on campus and in nearby communities. A dedicated library at LPU provides another avenue for students from adopted and nearby villages to access books and educational resources.

Dr. Ashok Kumar Mittal, Member of Parliament, Rajya Sabha, and Founder Chancellor of LPU, said that the purpose of education must ultimately be to expand opportunity. "Every Child Deserves the Opportunity to Learn, education becomes truly meaningful when it opens doors to opportunity. This is why LPU continues to focus on Corporate Social Responsibility initiatives and scholarships for deserving students from financially disadvantaged backgrounds, so that lack of resources does not become a barrier to education. Every child deserves the opportunity to learn, to dream and to believe that their circumstances do not have to define their future."

The University's community engagement has also connected education with wider public well being. During the Pulse Polio Immunization Drive conducted in collaboration with the Civil Surgeon, Jalandhar, LPU-NSS volunteers supported the administration of polio drops to children below five years of age at key locations. The effort reflected the larger idea behind community service at the University that meaningful education and social development often go hand in hand.

For LPU, programmes such as GyanDeep represent a larger understanding of what a university can contribute to society. Its students are not only learning inside classrooms but are also being given opportunities to take what they know into communities, share their skills and understand the realities faced by children who have fewer educational resources.

This approach is also reflected in the University's commitment to the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals, particularly those relating to poverty, quality education and reduced inequalities. On a day dedicated globally to literacy, GyanDeep presents a simple idea with a larger implication, sometimes, improving literacy does not require building another classroom, it requires taking a teacher, a book, a computer or simply the willingness to teach to a child who has been waiting for that opportunity.
